item.title: Hidden clues could help predict a woman’s breast cancer risk years in advance
item.description: An AI tool developed at NYU Langone Health analyzes years of 3D mammograms to predict breast cancer risk up to five years before a diagnosis.
item.content:encoded:
An artificial intelligence (AI) tool could help doctors predict a woman's risk of developing breast cancer years in advance, according to new research.

In a new study, published in the American Journal of Roentgenology, researchers at NYU Langone Health and its Perlmutter Cancer Center tested an AI model designed to estimate a woman's risk of developing breast cancer within five years.

The tool looks at several years of a woman's 3D mammograms to track changes in breast tissue over time, rather than looking only at the latest scan, according to the researchers.

NEW ALZHEIMER'S BLOOD TEST PREDICTS WHO IS LIKELY TO DEVELOP DEMENTIA IN 5 TO 10 YEARS

The model was developed using more than 313,000 mammograms from more than 161,000 women, according to the study.

Connie Lehman, a Massachusetts-based breast imaging specialist and professor of radiology at Harvard Medical School who was not involved in the study, told Fox News Digital that AI could help identify women whose increased risk might otherwise go unnoticed.

"For decades, as a doctor and breast imaging specialist, I have cared for women who were shocked by a breast cancer diagnosis," Lehman said. "Again and again, I heard: 'How can this be? No one in my family has had breast cancer.'"

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Traditional risk assessments can consider factors such as family history and genetic mutations, while AI can look for additional clues within a woman's breast tissue, according to Lehman.

"A mammogram can tell us more than whether cancer is visible today — it can also provide information about a woman's risk of developing cancer in the years ahead," she said.

That information could eventually help doctors tailor breast cancer screening to a woman's individual risk, Lehman said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

Women identified as being at increased risk could discuss additional screening, such as MRI, with their health care providers, while women at average risk may continue with routine mammograms, according to Lehman.

The technology could also analyze mammograms a woman has already had, meaning the added risk information would not require another imaging exam or additional radiation, she noted.

Lehman cautioned that an AI risk score is not a cancer diagnosis and cannot predict with certainty whether a woman will develop the disease.

"A higher score can prompt a conversation with your health care provider about additional screening and risk-reduction options," she said. "A lower score does not eliminate risk or replace regular mammography."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The NYU model remains a research tool and is not FDA-authorized for clinical use, according to Lehman.

The researchers also noted that more testing is needed. The study used mammograms from NYU Langone hospitals and imaging equipment from one manufacturer.

The team plans to test the model using data from other medical centers and different 3D mammography systems, according to NYU Langone.

Fox News Digital reached out to the researchers for comment.

item.title: Lane Kiffin is staring down disastrous year one as offseason pleas for patience fall on deaf ears
item.description: Lane Kiffin's $40 million LSU Tigers roster faces mounting pressure after a stunning 35-34 loss to Will Stein's Kentucky Wildcats at Kroger Field.
item.content:encoded:
One of the biggest, most consequential games of the season so far took place in Tuscaloosa on Saturday night — in the wake of a hurricane, no less — but a different game was taking place about six hours north on I-65 that was also rife with national implications.

The Kentucky Wildcats and LSU Tigers played an all-time classic of a college football game this weekend, with Big Blue Nation pulling off a stunner, downing the top-ten Tigers 35-34 in front of a sold-out crowd at Kroger Field.

What this means for the Wildcats and first-year head coach Will Stein can't be overstated, as the new Kentucky head man now has two top-ten wins in his first six games on the job, and the arrow is pointing straight up in the Bluegrass State as of mid-October.

KENTUCKY COACH WILL STEIN TELLS WILDCATS PLAYERS 'IF YOU DON'T BELIEVE IN WHAT WE'RE DOING, YOU ARE HIGH'

But on the opposite sideline on Saturday night, LSU head coach Lane Kiffin was left with more questions than answers as the honeymoon phase in Baton Rouge likely came to a screeching halt.

Things aren't exactly up in smoke for Kiffin in his first year on the Bayou.

LANE KIFFIN KNOWS THERE AREN’T EXCUSES AT LSU. NOW COMES THE TEST OF MAKING IT WORTH THE PRICE OF ADMISSION

The Tigers are 4-2 with wins over Clemson and Texas A&M and are still in the AP top-25 as of this afternoon, falling from 10th to 22nd.

However, this probably isn't how anyone in purple and gold expected the season to go when they imagined the infinite possibilities back in August.

LSU had one of the most expensive rosters in the country, estimated at around $40 million, as well as a coaching staff many considered to be the best in the country, top to bottom.

The loss to Ole Miss three weeks ago stung, but was not unexpected.

The Rebels were favored and had the benefit of playing at home, and the added context of Kiffin returning to the program, he turned his back on to go coach in The Boot made that a tough one to win.

But losing to a first-time head coach at a program that you have a marked talent and resources advantage over is a tough pill to swallow.

WHO'S REALLY PLAYED THE BEST THUS FAR THROUGH THE FIRST HALF OF THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL SEASON?

And to top it all off, the Tigers took a massive L on the recruiting trail on Sunday when their flip target, five-star wide receiver and former Texas commit Easton Royal, opted to head to Gainesville and play for the Gators.

Losing a five-star prospect to an in-conference rival is never fun, but when you consider Royal is from nearby New Orleans and was long thought to be an LSU lean even while committed to the Longhorns, it makes it even harder to accept.

Sure, signing day is still two months away, but that's a prospect you'd rather hold onto than try to flip in the 11th hour.

Things don't get any easier for the Bayou Bengals, either.

Their October features a visit from top-20 Mississippi State as well as a trip to Jordan Hare to play Auburn.

Then they play three consecutive top-15 teams in November (Alabama, Texas, and at Tennessee) before a relative break on the road against Arkansas to end the season.

It's not inconceivable to envision another two losses in that stretch.

If you asked an LSU fan over the summer if 8-4 was an acceptable year one, they would have laughed in your face, and they would have had every right to do so.

Between Kiffin, the coaching staff, and the roster, this is easily a $150 million operation, and 8-4 and a trip to the Duke's Mayo Bowl isn't going to cut the mustard.

Kiffin famously pleaded for patience during spring practice, but unfortunately for him, in this day and age of NIL and the transfer portal, patience no longer exists at a tier one program like LSU.

My confidence in Kiffin's ability to win at LSU has not waned.

First years are rife with trial and error, and not every coach can have a Curt Cignetti-type start to their tenure.

Kiffin and his staff will figure out what works and what doesn't on this roster, and trim the fat where necessary.

As long as the powers that be continue to fund this thing, LSU and Kiffin will be fine.

But Saturday night's loss to Kentucky raises those same uncomfortable questions I already discussed.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Why couldn't a $40 million roster and one of the hottest coaches in the country beat a lower-tier SEC team.

If Will Stein can do it in year one, why can't Lane Kiffin?

I'm not here to answer those questions or even argue their validity, but this is what folks in Baton Rouge will no doubt be thinking this week.

I've said it before, and I will say it again, the honeymoon in Death Valley is over.

Now we get to find out if Kiffin is really made for this gig.

item.title: GOP senator calls for FCC probe of ABC News over Trump sons-Anduril 'political hit job'
item.description: Sen. Bernie Moreno urged the FCC to investigate ABC News over a retracted report linking Donald Trump Jr. and Anduril Industries to government contracts.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Bernie Moreno, R-OH, called on the Federal Communications Commission on Saturday to launch a formal investigation into ABC News after the network deleted and substantially revised a report involving President Donald Trump's sons and defense contractor Anduril Industries, accusing the Disney-owned network of publishing false information that could damage a major investment in his home state.

In a letter to FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, Moreno demanded accountability for the network's report and questioned whether ABC News violated its obligations as a broadcaster.

"Thus, I urge the Commission to open a formal investigation into ABC News's political hit job. We must know who signed off on the publication of this false story, who may have asked to profit from the attack, and whether ABC News's conduct violated its obligations as a licensee," Moreno said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Moreno's office for additional comment but a spokesperson for the senator declined to elaborate on the allegations.

FCC CALLS IN DISNEY-OWNED ABC STATIONS FOR EARLY LICENSE REVIEW IN WAKE OF JIMMY KIMMEL CONTROVERSY

The senator's request followed ABC News' decision to remove a report examining investments tied to Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump. The original Wednesday article claimed companies connected to the president's sons had secured billions in government contracts, including through venture capital firm 1789 Capital.

Moreno specifically challenged the original report's characterization of Anduril's financing, arguing that the network had misrepresented the company's investment activity and unfairly associated the Trump family with federal contracting decisions.

"ABC News appears under broadcast licenses issued by the FCC. These licenses are a privilege, not a right. They require service of the public interest," he said.

FCC BOSS BRENDAN CARR MAINTAINS EARLY ABC LICENSE RENEWAL IS ABOUT DEI PROBE, NOT JIMMY KIMMEL CONTROVERSY

The controversy centered on ABC News' original claim that 1789 Capital, where Trump Jr. serves as a partner, acquired a major strike in Anduril through a $2.5 billion investment. The figure instead represented Anduril's broader fundraising round, while 1789 Capital's investment was approximately $50 million.

ABC News republished a substantially revised article Friday, acknowledging errors involving investments, government contracts and the chronology of events. The updated version also clarified that Trump Jr. does not serve on the firm's investment decision-making committee. The report was republished Friday with a new headline, revised byline and an editor's note acknowledging factual errors involving company investments, government contracts and the chronology of events.

Moreno also emphasized the economic stakes for Ohio, where Anduril is developing its Arsenal-1 manufacturing facility. The company has announced plans to invest nearly $1 billion in the project, which is expected to create more than 4,000 jobs.

DISNEY SUES FCC OVER ‘RETALIATORY CAMPAIGN AGAINST ABC,’ SEEKS TO BLOCK EARLY RENEWAL PROCEEDINGS

In his letter, Moreno accused ABC News of undermining public confidence in journalism while potentially harming a major employer in the state.

"The American people, and the workers in Ohio whose jobs were put at risk by this reporting, deserve answers and accountability," Moreno said.

The investigation request comes amid an ongoing legal dispute between Disney and the FCC over the commission's early review of ABC-owned television station licenses. Disney argued that the review threatens constitutionally protected editorial independence, while the FCC defended its actions as regulatory oversight.

Fox News Digital reached out to the FCC but did not immediately receive a response.

A network source for ABC News told Fox News Digital, "We always review every situation in a thorough and thoughtful manner and will not be providing further comment at this time."

item.title: Toddler stabbed in face, suspect previously deemed unfit for trial in attacks on 2 children: report
item.description: Nelson Blanco allegedly stabbed a toddler at a Rhode Island school bus stop, decades after being found incompetent to stand trial for knifing two boys.
item.content:encoded:
A stranger allegedly stabbed a toddler in the face as she sat in her stroller at a Rhode Island school bus stop, years after he was accused of knifing two other children and found incompetent to stand trial.

The child’s fight for survival has brought renewed scrutiny into the suspect’s past, including an attack on two children more than two decades ago and repeated findings that he was incompetent to stand trial.

Nelson Blanco, 46, is accused of stabbing the 2-year-old girl and her mother Wednesday afternoon near Broad and Public streets in Providence, police said.

SOUTH CAROLINA MOM ACCUSED OF KNIFE ATTACK ON YOUNG CHILDREN; 6-YEAR-OLD MAY LOSE ARM: SHERIFF'S OFFICE

The toddler was taken to Hasbro Children’s Hospital in critical condition. Her mother, who suffered a stab wound to the shoulder, was treated and released, according to local reporting.

The mother was waiting with her daughter for her other children to get off a school bus when Blanco allegedly approached and made insulting comments, Providence Police Chief Oscar Perez said, according to WPRI.

ANGEL MOM SAYS BLUE STATE DAS ARE PUTTING ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT CRIMINALS BEFORE PUBLIC SAFETY

She crossed the street with the stroller to get away, but Blanco approached again and allegedly attacked the child with a knife, police said, noting there was no evidence he knew either victim.

Surveillance video showed the mother and daughter attempting to move away before Blanco grabbed the stroller and struck the child repeatedly, Boston 25 News reported.

A bystander tried to intervene, but Blanco allegedly attempted to stab that person before fleeing, according to the outlet.

Officers found Blanco hiding in the basement of a nearby home and recovered a knife from a panel box, police said. Authorities said he admitted to the stabbings during questioning.

CALIFORNIA STABBING VICTIM'S FRIEND BLASTS 'FAILED' JUSTICE SYSTEM OVER ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT SUSPECT'S RELEASE

Blanco allegedly told detectives he stopped the attack because he was on a main street, according to a police report obtained by WPRI.

"If I was on a side street, I would have killed them. Both of them," he said, according to the outlet.

PROSECUTORS SAY CHARLOTTE TRAIN STABBING CASE WON'T BE DISMISSED REGARDLESS OF COMPETENCY RULING

Blanco faces six charges, including two counts police identified as assault with intent to commit murder, felony assault, breaking and entering into an occupied dwelling of a person 60 or older, and two weapons charges.

No plea was entered during his Thursday appearance in Rhode Island’s 6th Division District Court. The court referred him to the public defender and requested an evaluation, according to court records reviewed by Fox News Digital.

VIOLENT TRANSIT ATTACKS IN ATLANTA, NEW YORK AND CHARLOTTE FUEL CALLS FOR TOUGHER TRACKING OF REPEAT OFFENDERS

WPRI reported Blanco is being held without bail pending a competency hearing later this month.

His arrest brought back painful memories for Andy Lopez and Dave Belony, who told WPRI they were 6 and 7 years old when Blanco attacked them while they played in Lopez’s backyard on Sept. 27, 2003.

CHARLOTTE REPEAT OFFENDER CHARGED WITH KILLING MAN HOURS AFTER RELEASE ON BOND

Belony said he recognized Blanco immediately when he saw his booking photo on social media Wednesday night.

"I knew it was him, because I will always remember that face," he told the station. "My heart dropped, and it truly felt like my world had stopped."

Court records reviewed by Fox News Digital show Blanco faced two felony assault charges and a charge of possessing a knife or firearm during a crime, stemming from the 2003 incident.

BANK OF AMERICA EXEC KILLED IN RANDOM TIMES SQUARE STABBING LAID TO REST AS HUNDREDS MOURN YOUNG MOM

The docket documents repeated findings that Blanco was incompetent to stand trial from September 2004 through March 2006. Multiple entries state, "Defendant Remains Incompetent." The case remains listed as "under review" in the court portal.

More recently, Blanco was found incompetent to stand trial in July in a separate domestic violence case, WPRI reported. A judge accepted a doctor’s recommendation allowing him to remain in outpatient treatment because he was considered unlikely to endanger the community or himself at that time.

Lopez and Belony said the earlier attack left them with injuries and trauma that have followed them into adulthood.

They told WPRI they were playing with Lopez’s brother when Blanco emerged from a shed behind the house where he had been living.

"He didn’t say a word," Belony recalled. "His face was blank and he was just staring at us."

Belony said Blanco charged at him, trapping him near a tree. He curled into a ball and covered his head as Blanco stabbed him.

DEMOCRATIC BOSTON COUNCILOR RIPS 'SOFT-ON-CRIME' POLICIES AFTER SUSPECTED GUNMAN'S VIOLENT PAST REVEALED

Blanco then turned toward Lopez, the men said.

"My brother yelled at me to run, and I was trying to run but my body just froze," Lopez told WPRI. "He stabbed me twice in the eye — the first time it was blurry, and then the second time I couldn’t see anything."

Both children were rushed to Hasbro Children’s Hospital. Their recovery took three months and included at least three surgeries each, they told the outlet.

Lopez was left permanently blind in his left eye, an injury he said derailed his dreams of becoming a police officer or truck driver.

"Most of the opportunities I wanted to have in life are gone," he said. "I’m very grateful I’m alive, but my life is restricted."

Belony said he was stabbed at least five times in his stomach, back and ribs and continues to struggle emotionally.

The men said learning about the latest attack left them devastated for the mother and toddler, and determined to speak out.

"It’s frustrating for us, not only because of what happened to us, but because it has happened to others," Lopez told WPRI. "He was given a chance 23 years ago, and 23 years later, he did the same thing."

"We want justice for the victims," Belony said. "What is it going to take for him to be held accountable for his actions?"

Fox News Digital reached out to the Providence Police Department and the Rhode Island attorney general’s office for comment.

item.title: 'I lost us that game': Nick Sirianni makes decision that opened door to a Jacksonville Jaguars comeback win
item.description: Nick Sirianni says he cost the Eagles the game after a short kickoff let the Jaguars set up Cam Little's stunning walk-off 57-yard field goal.
item.content:encoded:
NFL head coaches often take responsibility for not helping their team, but usually when they seek the blame for losing, they are often covering for someone else's mistake. Then we have Philadelphia Eagles coach Nick Sirianni.

He took the blame for the Eagles' walk-off field goal loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday because, well, it was indeed ultimately on him.

Why?

Because the Eagles blew the game in London by not kicking the ball into the end zone while clinging to a 17-16 lead with only eight seconds to play.

JALEN HURTS CURSES AT RECEIVER IN VIRAL HOT-MIC MOMENT DURING EAGLES' COLLAPSE AGAINST RAMS

Down two points, the Jaguars returned the kick that was short of the end zone 53 yards to the Eagles' 39-yard line. The runback took seven seconds.

And with one second remaining left, Cam Little, who has a kicking leg like a howitzer, connected on a game-winning 57-yard field goal.

That left the Eagles with their third loss of the season.

And Sirianni with mushy peas on his face.

"I lost us that game and that's what I said to our guys," Sirianni admitted in his post-game news conference.

"What hurt there is that the guys fought so hard, and I don’t make the decision that I should make at the end of the game and I cost us that game, and I put that fully on me."

Sirianni was not in the mood to accept other reasons the Eagles lost.

"At the end of the day, I didn’t make the right decision, and it cost us the game," he said. "You know, and so there’s no other way around it. There’s nothing really else to say about that. It’s just I didn’t do my job good enough in that situation."

It was obviously not all Sirianni's fault. The Eagles' kickoff coverage unit was leaky from the start of the game to the end.

And maybe kicker Jake Elliott should have kicked the ball into the end zone of his own accord. He is a veteran and should understand the situation.

But, people in Philly, raise your hand if you disagree that Sirianni had a brain lock.

Waiting for a hand to rise.

Still waiting.

Nobody.

Sirianni is going to carry this for a while because Eagles fans are not too forgiving. And neither is the Philadelphia media.

"It’s just like you would feel if you missed a free throw at the end of the game, or if you had a drop," Sirianni said. "I’ve been in both of those places. And those ones stick with you, and that will stick with me for a long time.

"... Yeah, that one will hurt for a long time. I still think about those other things that have, I’ve lost games for us in the past as far as, you know, when I played."

MIKE TOMLIN POINTS OUT DALLAS COWBOYS 'NEGLIGENT' COACHING MISTAKES AND PUT HIMSELF IN CONVERSATION TO TAKE JOB NEXT YEAR

There are two issues with what Sirianni just said:

First, it is the coach's job to stop the bleeding. His team already allowed a fourth-quarter loss to the Rams last week to become a two-week disaster and grow into a three-game losing skid overall.

Second, if Sirianni's message to his team is that this loss will stick with him a long time, that is exactly the wrong message to send.

What's up with these NFC East coaches and last second kickoffs?

A couple of weeks ago, the Dallas Cowboys blew a game against the Baltimore Ravens in the final seconds when coach Brian Schottenheimer did the exact opposite of what Sirianni did on Sunday by sending the kickoff into the end zone, which didn't tick any time off the clock.

The Ravens used seven seconds to get into field goal range.

So Sirianni did something different and still got burned.

The crazy part of this is that Sirianni says he saw that Dallas situation on tape.

"I watched a ton of those situations after that Dallas game and, again, just didn’t make the right decision in this particular case," he said.

item.title: Mojtaba Khamenei defies ‘malicious’ attacks as US Army zeroes in on Iran’s 350,000 troops
item.description: Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei claimed U.S. and Israeli strikes failed to weaken Iran's military, as the U.S. Army released a new threat guide.
item.content:encoded:
Iranian Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei claimed Oct. 8 that U.S. and Israeli strikes had failed to undermine Iran's domestic security forces, praising police personnel for resisting attacks launched in February under Operations Epic Fury and Roaring Lion.

Khamenei's remarks on X also came as the U.S. Army released a new battlefield identification guide to help American troops recognize members of Iran's conventional military, known as the Artesh, whose ground forces were estimated by the Jerusalem Institute for Strategy and Security in June at 350,000 personnel.

"The criminal US-Zionist enemy's desperate efforts and malicious attacks on the pillars of social order and security, which are unparalleled throughout history, have not caused the courageous personnel of the Police Force to waver even a fraction in their mission," Khamenei wrote in a statement.

Khamenei specifically praised Iran's Law Enforcement Command, known as FARAJA, accusing the United States and Israel of targeting the institution responsible for maintaining domestic order.

"The focus and persistence of the criminal US-Zionist enemy in striking at the Police Force at its various levels, from its highest command levels down to those who are on the frontline, has only served to underscore the paramount importance of this institution more than ever," he wrote.

IRAN PROVES THAT IT MIGHT CHANGE ITS MILITARY LEADERS, BUT IT’S NOT CHANGING STRATEGY

Iran's security apparatus comprises three principal branches: the Artesh, responsible primarily for conventional territorial defense; the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), tasked with protecting the Islamic Republic and projecting military power; and FARAJA, responsible for domestic law enforcement and internal security.

IRAN’S GUTTED RANKS LEAVE LOYALISTS FILLING CRITICAL POSTS — WITH ONE GLARING PROBLEM

FARAJA, commanded by Brig. Gen. Ahmadreza Radan, is responsible for maintaining public order, enforcing the country's laws and responding to civil unrest.

According to Iran Human Rights Monitor, the force has evolved into a powerful internal security institution involved in suppressing anti-government demonstrations, monitoring political activity and enforcing the regime's ideological restrictions.

IRAN INSTALLS NEW WAR CHIEFS AS TEHRAN SIGNALS ‘PROLONGED CONFRONTATION,’ EXPERT WARNS

Radan has also been sanctioned by the United States for his role in human rights abuses.

The Treasury Department designated him in September 2010, citing his responsibility for beatings, killings and arbitrary arrests of protesters following Iran's disputed 2009 presidential election.

Khamenei also called for strengthening FARAJA on Oct. 8 through additional personnel, equipment and technology, including the use of artificial intelligence for data analysis.

AFTER 47 YEARS OF CONFRONTING IRAN, DOES AMERICA HAVE A STRATEGY FOR ENDING THIS WAR?

His remarks come as the U.S. Army's Training and Transformation Command published a "Know the Threat" recognition guide Sept. 24, highlighted by Defense News on Oct. 9.

The guide shows an Iranian special forces soldier and identifies weapons American troops could encounter, including AKM rifles, Iranian-made Masaf-2 rifles, German-designed G3 rifles, MG3 machine guns and RPG-7 rocket-propelled grenade launchers.

The Artesh, Iran's regular military, is separate from the IRGC and its affiliated Basij militia. Its forces operate across four branches: the Ground Forces, Navy, Air Force and Air Defense Force.

A June assessment by the Jerusalem Institute for Strategy and Security estimated the Artesh's Ground Forces at approximately 350,000 personnel, including 220,000 conscripts.

The report found that the Artesh had suffered severe losses across its air, naval and air defense components during the opening phase of the U.S.-Israeli military campaign, while its ground forces remained structurally intact because there had been no ground invasion.

TRUMP OPENS HORMUZ UNDER FIRE WITH ‘PROJECT FREEDOM’ AS IRAN WARNS OF ATTACKS

The Artesh is commanded by Maj. Gen. Amir Hatami, a former Iranian defense minister who assumed command in June 2025.

Aside from Khamenei, Hatami issued his own warning Oct. 6, claiming Iran's adversaries faced "historic confusion" after failing to halt military production during the conflict.

Hatami also claimed that Iranian defense production continued despite American and Israeli attacks, saying the country's military production lines had continued operating during the conflict.

The extent of Iran's military recovery remains unclear. The Jerusalem Institute for Strategy and Security assessed in June that the country's conventional air, naval and air defense forces had suffered severe damage during the conflict.

President Donald Trump, meanwhile, said Oct. 8 that Washington would not resume military strikes against Iran before the Nov. 3 midterm elections, citing "productive discussions" between the two countries.

item.title: Luxury hotel favored by Kennedys, Grace Kelly cracks down on influencer photo shoots
item.description: The famed Hotel du Cap-Eden-Roc on the French Riviera bans photo shoots without permission as influencers and social media habits clash with guest privacy at the luxury property.
item.content:encoded:
A well-known luxury hotel is cracking down on photo shoots and cellphone use as some visitors' social media habits clash with other guests' desire for privacy.

Hotel du Cap-Eden-Roc has introduced rules aimed at limiting disruptive photography and preserving privacy at the property.

The famed hotel on the French Riviera in Antibes, France, has long attracted prominent guests — with members of the Kennedy family among those who have spent time in its rooms, suites and villas. 

ONCE-HIDDEN COASTAL TOWN FACING DISRUPTION AS SOCIAL MEDIA INFLUENCERS TRANSFORM LOCAL LIFE

Grace Kelly, Orson Welles, Elizabeth Taylor, F. Scott Fitzgerald, Ernest Hemingway, Cole Porter and Pablo Picasso are among the others who would also frequent the property.

The hotel has also hosted high-profile celebrations, including the 2023 wedding of Sofia Richie Grainge, daughter of musician Lionel Richie.

Under the hotel's current policy, photo shoots are prohibited on the property unless guests receive permission from management.

"To preserve the peace and privacy of all our guests, photo shoots are not permitted on the property," the hotel states on its website.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Guests with special photography requests are directed to the hotel's concierge, who can review the request and, when appropriate, connect people with the property's photographer, according to the website.

The restrictions come amid growing concerns over how some visitors are using the hotel, according to Travel Weekly.

Hotel manager Sophie Volant told the outlet that some people visiting for lunch were spending more time taking photos than enjoying their meals.

"We have a lot of loyal, repeat guests who don't see this hotel as a hotel — they see Hotel du Cap as their summer home," said Volant.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

Some non-hotel guests have been said to arrive with bags of clothing and jewelry, changing outfits multiple times while using the property for lengthy photo shoots, according to Travel Weekly.

Volant said most guests have welcomed the new rules — with some even encouraging the hotel to enforce them more strictly, the article noted. 

The rules have also drawn reactions from travelers online after one guest shared a photo of the card outlining the hotel's policies.

"Absolutely stunning property, but I think social media and influencers ruined it for me," one user wrote.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Others agreed that setting expectations for guests was necessary.

"Those rules shouldn't need to be printed but sadly need to be," another person commented.

Fox News Digital reached out to Hotel du Cap-Eden-Roc for further details and comment.

Among the amenities at the hotel today, according to its website, are conference facilities, indoor pool, sauna, solarium, fitness center, spa, massage room, hot tub, library and bicycle rental.

The property also offers hiking and horseback riding.  

The property spans 22.5 acres of private parkland, pine trees and palm gardens overlooking the Mediterranean Sea.

item.title: Will Stein's dad storms the field after Kentucky's upset win over LSU in beautiful college football scene
item.description: Video captures Will Stein's father slowly walking onto the field with arms raised as Kentucky fans stormed the turf after the overtime upset of LSU.
item.content:encoded:
There were quite a few happy people in Lexington, Kentucky, on Saturday night after the Wildcats upset LSU in an overtime thriller, but it's hard to imagine anyone being happier than Will Stein's father, and there is video evidence to support it.

After LSU needed just two plays to score on its first possession in overtime to jump out to a 34-27 lead, the Wildcats were forced to respond, and respond they did. Running back CJ Baxter punched it into the end zone, which left Stein with a decision to make: kick the extra point and head into a second overtime or go for two and try to end the game in front of your home crowd.

Stein opted for the latter, and it paid off.

KENTUCKY COACH WILL STEIN TELLS WILDCATS PLAYERS 'IF YOU DON'T BELIEVE IN WHAT WE'RE DOING, YOU ARE HIGH'

After a controversial flag on the first two-point conversion that was negated by a Kentucky timeout, quarterback Kenny Minchey trotted onto the field and walked right up the middle into the end zone to send Big Blue Nation into a frenzy with a 35-34 victory.

It was Kentucky's second consecutive 35-34 overtime win after the Wildcats came back to win at South Carolina seven days prior.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Given the win over the No. 10 team in the nation and it marking Kentucky's first victory over LSU in Lexington since 2007, fans celebrated accordingly and stormed the field.

As thousands of Kentucky fans leaped over the walls of the stadium and sprinted onto the turf, Stein's father got in on the fun as well, but in a different fashion.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Surrounded by pure and joyful chaos, Stein slowly walked onto the turf with his arms in the air in awe of the scene unfolding in front of him.

Each college football season creates its own set of magical moments, but a father basking in a moment his son just managed to pull off at the school he grew up being a die-hard fan of is about as special as it gets.

Stein rushed the field when Kentucky upset LSU in 2007, and for him to deliver another field storm as the Wildcats newest head coach against the same team in front of his old man is objectively awesome.
